issues: Nit: /root/batch9-pam-security.tar is gzip-compressed (tar -czf) but named .tar. Extraction works because both sides pass -z. Rename to .tar.gz in a later batch if you want.

Nit: the ERR trap is not inherited by shell functions (no set -E). A bare command failing inside active_eq, active_bare or write_profiles would exit under set -e without running the revert, which leaves only the 300s timer as protection. That timer is not armed until the end. The realistic failure points (grep, apt, pam-auth-update, chage, validation) are already guarded with explicit reverts or run at top level. Adding set -E would close this.

Nit: Ubuntu 26.04 may ship sudo-rs. If `sudo -n -v` as root behaves differently there, PASTE 1 stops with STOP-root-sudo-n and reverts, and PASTE 2 stops before disarming the timer. Both are safe failures. They would only be a nuisance, and the check proves nothing about aj anyway, so it could be dropped.

Nit: the revert helper runs pam-auth-update from a systemd service with no tty. Exporting DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive at the top of the helper would remove any chance of a debconf prompt. A failure there is already non-fatal (WARN-pam-auth-update) and the tar extract has restored the stock stack.
Nit: 5.4.1.1 and 5.4.1.5 only cover aj and new accounts. Other accounts that have a password could still be flagged on re-audit. The doc already says this.
